{
  "tool": "code_write_file",
  "args": {
    "path": "ci-cd/cloudbuild.yaml.template",
    "content": "# cloudbuild.yaml.template
# This template defines a Google Cloud Build pipeline for containerizing and deploying microservices to Cloud Run.
# It is designed to be reusable and parameterized for different services and environments.

# --- GLOBAL VARIABLES ---
# These variables can be overridden at runtime or by service-specific cloudbuild.yaml files.
substitutions:
  _SERVICE_NAME: default-service
  _PROJECT_ID: ${PROJECT_ID}
  _REGION: us-central1
  _DOCKERFILE_PATH: Dockerfile
  _BUILD_CONTEXT: .
  _IMAGE_NAME: gcr.io/${_PROJECT_ID}/${_SERVICE_NAME}
  _TAG_NAME: ${_IMAGE_NAME}:${_COMMIT_SHA:0:7}
  _RUNTIME_IMAGE: gcr.io/cloud-run-containers/distroless/python3-debian11 # Example: use a distroless base for Python
  _BUILD_IMAGE: python:3.9-slim-buster # Example: use Python for build stage
  _SERVICE_ACCOUNT: projects/${_PROJECT_ID}/members/service-${_PROJECT_NUMBER}@gcp-sa-cloudbuild.iam.gserviceaccount.com # Cloud Build service account
  _MEMORY: 512Mi # Default Cloud Run memory allocation
  _CPU: 1 # Default Cloud Run CPU allocation
  _CONCURRENCY: 80 # Default Cloud Run concurrency
  _MIN_INSTANCES: 0 # Default Cloud Run min instances
  _MAX_INSTANCES: 10 # Default Cloud Run max instances
  _ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED: 'false' # Default Cloud Run allow unauthenticated traffic
  _ENV_VARS: "" # Comma-separated list of key=value environment variables (e.g., FOO=bar,BAZ=qux)
  _SECRETS: "" # Comma-separated list of secret key=value pairs (e.g., FOO=SECRET_ID:VERSION,BAR=ANOTHER_SECRET:LATEST)


steps:

# --- STEP 1: Build and Tag Docker Image ---
# Uses Kaniko (default builder in Cloud Build) to build the Docker image.
# Dynamic Dockerfile and build context allow flexibility per service.
- id: 'Build and Tag Image'
  name: 'gcr.io/cloud-builders/docker'
  args: [
    'build',
    '-f', '${_DOCKERFILE_PATH}',
    '--build-arg', 'BUILD_IMAGE=${_BUILD_IMAGE}',
    '--build-arg', 'RUNTIME_IMAGE=${_RUNTIME_IMAGE}',
    '-t', '${_IMAGE_NAME}:${_COMMIT_SHA:0:7}',
    '-t', '${_IMAGE_NAME}:latest',
    '${_BUILD_CONTEXT}'
  ]

# --- STEP 2: Push Docker Image to Google Container Registry (GCR) ---
# Pushes the newly built image to GCR, making it available for Cloud Run deployment.
- id: 'Push Image to GCR'
  name: 'gcr.io/cloud-builders/docker'
  args: ['push', '${_IMAGE_NAME}:${_COMMIT_SHA:0:7}']


# --- STEP 3: Deploy to Google Cloud Run ---
# Deploys the container image to Cloud Run.
# Includes dynamic configuration for service name, region, environment variables, and secrets.
- id: 'Deploy to Cloud Run'
  name: 'gcr.io/google.com/cloudsdktool/cloud-sdk'
  entrypoint: 'bash'
  args:
    - '-c'
    - |
      gcloud run deploy ${_SERVICE_NAME} \
        --image=${_IMAGE_NAME}:${_COMMIT_SHA:0:7} \
        --platform=managed \
        --region=${_REGION} \
        --project=${_PROJECT_ID} \
        --memory=${_MEMORY} \
        --cpu=${_CPU} \
        --concurrency=${_CONCURRENCY} \
        --min-instances=${_MIN_INSTANCES} \
        --max-instances=${_MAX_INSTANCES} \
        --service-account=${_SERVICE_ACCOUNT} \
        $( [ "${_ALLOW_UNAUTHENTICATED}" = "true" ] && echo "--allow-unauthenticated" || echo "--no-allow-unauthenticated" ) \
        $( [ -n "${_ENV_VARS}" ] && echo "--set-env-vars=${_ENV_VARS}" || echo "" ) \
        $( [ -n "${_SECRETS}" ] && echo "--set-secrets=${_SECRETS}" || echo "" )

# --- ARTIFACTS ---
# Specifies which images are built and pushed by this pipeline.
images:
  - '${_IMAGE_NAME}:${_COMMIT_SHA:0:7}'
  - '${_IMAGE_NAME}:latest'

# NOTE:
# For triggering this pipeline:
# - Create a Cloud Build trigger that points to your repository and this cloudbuild.yaml.template.
# - Use substitutions to customize deployments (e.g., _SERVICE_NAME, _REGION, _ENV_VARS).
# - For secrets, ensure the Cloud Build service account has 'Secret Manager Secret Accessor' role.
#   Example usage for secrets:
#   --set-secrets=DB_PASSWORD=my-db-password:latest,API_KEY=my-api-key:1
# - For environment variables:
#   --set-env-vars=NODE_ENV=production,PORT=8080
"
  }
}
